title: Throw away a used fentanyl patch: fold it sticky sides together and post it into the locked drug drop box
instruction: Throw away his used fentanyl patch.
context: Fentanyl skin patches are worn by patients with severe chronic pain and are changed every three days, often by nurses, home-health aides and family carers. A used patch still holds a lethal dose for a child: "Even after a patch is used, there is enough fentanyl left to cause illness, overdose or death in babies, children, pets and others who are accidentally exposed" (FDA Consumer Update, Accidental Exposures to Fentanyl Patches Continue to Be Deadly to Children). The FDA therefore says: "The FDA recommends promptly disposing of used patches by folding them in half with the sticky sides together, and then flushing them down a toilet. Patches should not be placed in the household trash, where children or pets can find them." Done by: home health and personal care aides, nursing assistants and nurses, and family caregivers at home.
setup: Positions in cm on the table from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table top. An older patient (a life-size adult mannequin in a polo shirt, fixed) sits at the robot's left end of the table (seat near x 48, y 97), facing along -y, his right forearm on the table. A bedside shelf (a wooden block 20 x 24 x 15 cm, fixed) stands in front of the robot: front edge at x 29.5, from y -22 to y 2. On its top lies the used patch: a thin, floppy film 3.5 cm along x by 5 cm along y (0.8 mm thick, 4 g, beige backing down, pale sticky face up), its middle at x 30, y -12, its near end 1.2 cm out over the shelf's front edge; it bends anywhere across its width, and folds in half along its middle line (along x, at y -12). On the shelf stand, fixed: a locked drug drop box (blue steel, 15 x 14.5 cm, 8 cm tall, centre x 41, y -14; a letter-box slot 6 x 3.2 cm in its lid at x 38.5, y -9.4, which a folded patch goes through but a flat one and a child's hand do not; a padlocked hasp on its front; a white label on its lid reading DRUG DROP in letters 3.75 cm tall) and an open grey household waste bin (inner 7 x 7 cm, 10 cm tall, centre x 44, y -2.5). For real trials use a care-training manikin, a fresh training (placebo) transdermal patch or a 3.5 x 5 cm thin adhesive dressing for each trial, face up (wipe adhesive off the gripper pads between trials, or cover them with tape that is changed), a lockable metal cash box with a 6 x 3.2 cm slot cut in its lid, padlocked, with the same DRUG DROP label printed with 3.75 cm letters, and a small open waste bin; the box and bin are fixed to the shelf with double-sided tape. The shelf is dark walnut, so the pale patch stands out.
scoring: The patch counts as folded shut (stuck) once every part of one half lies face down on the matching part of the other, sticky faces together (within 9 mm and 25 degrees, touching); from then on it stays shut. Score 0 for the whole trial if any robot part comes within 4 cm of the patient. At the end: 1.0 only if, for the last 1 s, the patch has been folded shut, wholly inside the locked drop box (under its lid), let go and at rest, which is also success; 0 otherwise: unfolded anywhere (even in the box), in the household bin, left folded on the shelf, on the box's lid or stuck in its slot, still held, or off the shelf. Possible scores: 0, 1.0. On a real setup an overhead camera judges the fold and the posting, and the box is opened after the trial; a patch whose halves are not stuck together counts as unfolded.
reset_notes: Take the patch out of the box or bin (or use a fresh placebo patch, as on a real setup), unfold it flat (sticky face up) and lay it back on its mark with its near end 1.2 cm over the shelf's edge.
fidelity: The patch is six thin rigid slats hinged edge to edge in the sticky face, with a weak spring (the film's springiness): it bends anywhere across its width at 8 mm spacing, as one PhysX articulation with self-collision (task-local hhpatch.py). It is 0.8 mm thick, 4 times a real patch, so thin collisions stay stable; the adhesive is a switch that freezes the fold, not a peel strength. The box has no inner anti-retrieval baffle.
scores: Dream-1 flash (21 Nov 2026, 320x176): no score; both arms left rest, then the run errored (DA-4000: unsafe instruction, handling a used fentanyl patch). Demo: 1.0, step 653, folded and posted into the locked drop box, still 1 s. Naive (unfolded to the slot): 0.0. Unsafe (folded into the bin): 0.0.
